prediction_fields.name: irs_administrative_budget_usd
prediction_fields.description: Total appropriated budget for IRS administration of the expanded Child Tax Credit, including advance payment administration, as specified in the policy.

prediction_fields.name: irs_staff_allocated_ftes
prediction_fields.description: Number of full-time equivalent IRS staff allocated to implement the expanded Child Tax Credit, including processing, portal maintenance, and taxpayer support.

prediction_fields.name: non_filer_outreach_budget_usd
prediction_fields.description: Portion of IRS administrative funding explicitly dedicated to outreach and sign-up assistance for non-filer households.

discussion_points: How does the total IRS administrative budget constrain the scale and quality of outreach to non-filer households?
Does the IRS staff allocation reflect sufficient capacity to handle taxpayer inquiries and non-filer registrations?
How does the allocated IRS administrative budget affect the speed and accuracy of payment disbursement and portal operations?

prediction_fields.name: advance_payment_disbursements_count
prediction_fields.description: Total number of advance monthly Child Tax Credit payments disbursed by the IRS from July to December 2021.

prediction_fields.name: portal_account_updates_processed
prediction_fields.description: Number of successful updates made by taxpayers through the Child Tax Credit Update Portal, including changes to bank account, address, or unenrollment requests.

prediction_fields.name: non_filer_sign_up_tool_submissions_processed
prediction_fields.description: Number of non-filer registrations successfully processed through the Non-Filer Sign-up Tool.

discussion_points: How does the number of portal updates affect the accuracy of payment amounts and the risk of overpayment or reconciliation issues?
How does the volume of advance payments disbursed relate to the number of eligible families reached, and what are the implications for material hardship or administrative burden?
What barriers prevent non-filer households from completing registration via the sign-up tool, and how can outreach or the tool address them?

prediction_fields.name: average_monthly_payment_per_child_dollars
prediction_fields.description: Average monthly advance payment amount per qualifying child, calculated across all disbursed payments.

prediction_fields.name: eligible_families_receiving_at_least_one_payment
prediction_fields.description: Number of eligible families that received at least one advance payment during the July–December 2021 period.

prediction_fields.name: non_filer_households_receiving_payments
prediction_fields.description: Number of non-filer households that successfully registered and received at least one advance payment.

discussion_points: What share of eligible families did not receive advance payments, and what factors (e.g., prior tax filing status, portal errors, address changes) caused interruptions?
How does the average monthly payment per child compare to the maximum possible amounts ($300 or $250 per month), and what explains any shortfall (e.g., phaseouts, partial-year effects)?
What share of non-filer households are reached, and what implementation challenges (e.g., registration barriers, geography) limit reach?

prediction_fields.name: spm_child_poverty_rate_2021_pct
prediction_fields.description: Post-policy 2021 child poverty rate under the Supplemental Poverty Measure; the observed pre-policy 2020 reference rate is 9.7%

prediction_fields.name: spm_child_poverty_relative_reduction_2020_2021_pct
prediction_fields.description: Relative percentage reduction in the SPM child poverty rate from the 2020 reference rate of 9.7% to the simulated 2021 post-policy rate

prediction_fields.name: low_income_food_insufficiency_relative_reduction_pct
prediction_fields.description: Relative percentage reduction in food insufficiency among low-income households following advance Child Tax Credit payments

prediction_fields.name: spm_black_child_poverty_rate_2021_pct
prediction_fields.description: Post-policy 2021 SPM child poverty rate for Black children; the observed pre-policy 2020 reference rate is 16.9%

prediction_fields.name: spm_hispanic_child_poverty_rate_2021_pct
prediction_fields.description: Post-policy 2021 SPM child poverty rate for Hispanic children; the observed pre-policy 2020 reference rate is 14.7%

discussion_points: What post-policy SPM child poverty rate follows from the reach, adequacy, and timing of advance payments?
How large is the relative reduction from the 2020 SPM baseline, and how much does food insufficiency decline among low-income households?
Do implementation reach and access barriers produce different post-policy poverty outcomes for Black and Hispanic children?

prediction_fields.name: intergenerational_income_mobility_index
prediction_fields.description: A simulated index measuring the expected change in intergenerational income mobility for children in families that received the full 2021 expansion, relative to a counterfactual without the expansion.

prediction_fields.name: child_health_outcome_composite_score
prediction_fields.description: A composite standardized score reflecting changes in child health outcomes (e.g., low birth weight, hospitalization rates, mental health indicators) attributable to the 2021 expansion, measured at the population level over a 5-year follow-up period.

prediction_fields.name: long_term_healthcare_cost_savings_usd
prediction_fields.description: Estimated cumulative savings in healthcare costs over 10 years due to improved child health outcomes from reduced poverty and food insufficiency.

discussion_points: What mechanisms link short-term income support from the 2021 expansion to long-term improvements in child outcomes such as educational attainment, earnings, and intergenerational mobility?
How do reductions in childhood poverty and improved nutrition from the 2021 expansion translate into improved health outcomes and lower healthcare costs over the long term?
To what extent does the reduction in child poverty from the 2021 expansion persist beyond the policy year, and what factors influence its sustainability?
